A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAD-RAG study. Text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, attention analyses, efficiency measurements, and ablations, including additional model experiments in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds model comparisons, intervention visualizations, and failure-case experiments.

M1.justification: The dual-question input construction and attention-mixing procedure in Section 5, including Equations (2)–(5), remain unchanged. Testing additional model families does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: OK-VQA, E-VQA, and InfoSeek coverage is retained. Appendix J/Figure 13 adds a limited image-removed diagnostic scenario, testing whether retrieved text alone supports correct answers on selected failure cases.

E2.justification: Table 6 removes the closed-book comparator for Qwen3-VL-4B and Qwen3-VL-8B, retaining Vanilla RAG versus MAD-RAG. The comparator sets in the main benchmark and efficiency tables are unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix H substantially expands evaluated model configurations with Qwen2.5-VL-32B/72B, InternVL-3.5, Phi3-Vision, and GLM-4.5V. Appendix J also introduces an image-removal control. These are additional experiments; the previously reported splits, context construction, and decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B/Figure 8 adds MAD-RAG attention maps and answers for previously illustrated distraction cases. Appendix J/Figures 12–13 adds a substantive investigation of cases where MAD-RAG hurts, combining attention comparisons with image-removal controls. v1 reported aggregate regressions but lacked this investigation.

E5.justification: Both versions specify greedy decoding with seed 0. v2 adds no repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 6 adds results for five model configurations and removes six Qwen3 closed-book scores. For example, the new Qwen2.5-VL-72B E-VQA comparison reports 83.49% for Vanilla RAG and 86.13% for MAD-RAG. Figures 8 and 12–13 add qualitative outcomes. Tables 1–5 and 7 and the retained Qwen3 RAG results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, causal-mask formulation, and attention-mixing equations are unchanged. The new boundary-condition discussion is empirical and interpretive, without new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about attention distraction, the training-free intervention, headline accuracy gains, and recovery of up to 74.68% of failures. Additional model tests support the existing generalizability claim.

C2.justification: Appendix J newly identifies adequate underlying visual grounding as a boundary condition: mixing poorly grounded visual attention can disrupt correct text-supported answers. Separately, Appendix I strengthens 'best or comparable' all-layer performance to 'best,' although unchanged Table 7 still shows slightly better LLaVA results for other layer selections.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract newly provides a MAD-RAG code-repository link. Existing prompt templates, hardware statement, mixing weight, context-processing instructions, and baseline implementation details are retained; the PDFs do not establish the repository's actual contents.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds a short discussion citing four works on spatial attention and visual refocusing, and the expanded model experiments introduce corresponding model references. The central positioning against ALFAR and hallucination-mitigation methods remains unchanged; updates to retained references are bibliographic.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained. Limited additions include the related-work passage, qualitative-analysis cross-reference, new appendix sections, acknowledgments, and a generic impact statement, alongside author/header and citation-format edits.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from one to two columns, with extensive resizing and repositioning of displays. v2 adds Figures 8, 12, and 13 and redesigns Table 6 with separate model and method columns. The earlier appendix Figures 8–10 are retained as Figures 9–11.

improvement.justification: Expanded model validation and the illustrated failure analysis improve empirical support and explain regressions left unexplained in v1; the code pointer also improves reproducibility information. These benefits outweigh limited regressions: omitted closed-book comparisons, Table 6's inaccurate caption, and the overstated all-layer interpretation of Table 7. The core method and principal results remain unchanged.
